text:
sam: heads-up — customer 'Ferno' on a Dedicated pool (eu-west) reporting repeated 429s and large tail latency this morning. I see the autoscaler ricocheting (2 -> 6 -> 2) every ~8m on that pool.

sam: quick snapshot of the metric that triggered it:
```
autoscaler.decisions: [2026-03-15T09:12:10Z scale_up 2->6 reason=queue_depth>scale_threshold]
autoscaler.decisions: [2026-03-15T09:17:22Z scale_down 6->2 reason=stabilize_window_passed]
request.queue_depth.p50: 120 -> p95: 980 -> p50: 110 (within 6m)
pod.restarts: +4
```

rachel: ugh. looks like noisy bursts from a single tenant job + our scaler using raw queue_depth without smoothing. pinging @jordan and oncall.

jordan: on it. can you paste the tenant id and the pool name? also any auth/billing errors tied to the 429s?

sam: tenant: fer-873, pool: ded-eu-west-c2. 429s are token-limit style and upstream shows our gateway returning 429s with "capacity limit". billing-bot shows no quota change for the tenant.

support_tony: customer reported timeouts around 09:15 and 09:24. They said restarting their worker temporarily removed errors but then it came back. Suspect they have a periodic batch hitting the pool.

jordan: grabbing pod logs from the pool — seeing repeated prefetch-cache invalidations and KV cache misses around spike windows. Not seeing GPU OOMs. CPU usage per-pod is low (30-40%) but queue length per-pod jumps.

sam: hypothesis: autoscaler uses instantaneous queue depth per-pool, so a single tenant burst pushes it up -> scale up -> burst finishes -> scale down too fast -> cache cold -> burst repeats -> ricochet.

rachel: proposed immediate mitigations:
- increase scale_down.cooldown from 60s -> 180s
- add stabilization_window/p95 smoothing (2m) to decision metric
- pin critical customers to dedicated reserved set during peak hours

jordan: implemented a temporary scaling tweak on ded-eu-west-c2 (scale_down.cooldown=180s) and enabled a 2m exponential_moving_avg for queue_depth metric. Observing now: only one scale action in last 20m. :thumbsup:

sam: nice. can you add repro steps in the ticket so SRE and Support can test? I recorded sequence to reproduce with a synthetic burst client that sends 1k requests across tenants unevenly (script below).
```
# repro-client (pseudo)
for i in 1..600:
  if i % 90 == 0:
    send_burst(tenant=fer-873, q=200)
  else:
    send(tenant=other, q=1)
  sleep(0.5)
```

support_tony: adding that repro to the Ferno support ticket and asking them to run in staging. Also asked them for any cron jobs that align with the times.

rachel: long-term actions (backlog):
- metric smoothing by default for queue-based autoscalers
- add workload-aware scaling profiles (tenant burst detection + warm pools)
- observable: per-tenant contribution to queue metric (so we can detect noisy neighbor)
- consider pre-warm hooks for cache-sensitive workloads

billing-bot: note — because tenant did not exceed quota, there is no billing action. escalate to product for dedicated-reservation options.

oncall-bot: incident log created: INC-2026-032-fermoric. Assigned to sam/jordan. ETA for mitigation: 2h (temporary knobs). ETA for backlog tickets: 3w.

jordan: follow-up: after knobs applied, p95 latency for the pool dropped from 1.6s -> 0.38s and 429s dropped to zero in the last 12m. Will keep monitoring and roll a proper config change if stable.

sam: thanks all — leaving the temp change in place until we have a safer rollout. I'll create the PR for smoothing and stabilization docs. If anyone sees new ricochet behavior, call it out here and I'll escalate immediately.
